open_comment_speakers.name: Tim Thomas
open_comment_speakers.topic: Library parking issue, applauded the six month trial honor system, concerned about what happens in 6 months. Re: Firefighters, expressed appreciation for work but does not want to see additional staff cuts

open_comment_speakers.name: Marilynnne Tarrall
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke of the benefit of the initiative which would allow for 6 district representatives, 2 at large representatives and direct election of the Mayor.

open_comment_speakers.name: Adrian Sopher
open_comment_speakers.topic: also in support of the initiative. Spoke to the benefits of the initiative.

open_comment_speakers.name: Elisabeth Patterson
open_comment_speakers.topic: also speaking in favor of the Districting.

open_comment_speakers.name: Julie Cavalier
open_comment_speakers.topic: The Junior golf program at Flatirons golf course - concerned that elimination of 2 full time golf professionals will force the elimination of this program - urged Council to reconsider this action.

open_comment_speakers.name: Michael Steiner
open_comment_speakers.topic: YOAB annual grants award program. Thanks Council for its support and explained the grant process that resulted in tonight's recommendation

open_comment_speakers.name: Kevin Lander
open_comment_speakers.topic: outlined the specific programs to be funded if approved by Council

open_comment_speakers.name: Steve Pomerance
open_comment_speakers.topic: district initiative, stated he was not willing to give up 5 votes for Councilmembers. Re: CU South, raised concerns about the content of the memo, indicating that there seems to be numerous holes in both process and content

open_comment_speakers.name: Ruth Blackmore
open_comment_speakers.topic: agreed with comments from Steve Pomerance and also noted that the city and CU cannot go around the 1041 rules nor can any development occur until after the hydrology as directed by CCHE.

open_comment_speakers.name: Dave Albee
open_comment_speakers.topic: agreed that nothing should happen before completion of the hydrology study at CU South

open_comment_speakers.name: Claire Levy
open_comment_speakers.topic: CU South 1) Hydrology study must be completed 2) Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan needs to be upheld - include County and 3) 1041 rules must be maintained.

open_comment_speakers.name: Ellen Willis
open_comment_speakers.topic: CU south - don't put the cart before the horse Wait for the hydrology study.

open_comment_speakers.name: Doug Yager
open_comment_speakers.topic: CU South - disappointed with the current status of the project and the continuing secret meetings

open_comment_speakers.name: Jeanne Lavendar
open_comment_speakers.topic: very concerned about the road going in above Marshall Rd. Expressed grave concern that citizens have no voice

open_comment_speakers.name: Doretta Hultquist
open_comment_speakers.topic: CU South - agreed with all other speakers that the MOU in the agenda packet is a complete NO GO! Citizen input is non-existent

open_comment_speakers.name: Gilbert White
open_comment_speakers.topic: Federal standard for 100 year flood damage is no longer affective as is evident that more frequent flood damage is now occurring Wait for hydrology study

open_comment_speakers.name: Connie Mansour
open_comment_speakers.topic: opposed to lighting at the CU tennis courts indicating that it is visible from her house

open_comment_speakers.name: Jann Scott
open_comment_speakers.topic: Channel 54 - opposed to potential budget cuts noting that it would basically eliminate Public Access T.V

open_comment_speakers.name: Lynn Segal
open_comment_speakers.topic: opposed to CU South MOA - Everyone needs to stop and think

open_comment_speakers.name: Alison Buchell
open_comment_speakers.topic: summarized a host of issues related to the flawed MOA for CU South. Also indicated that the lack of public inclusion after being promised should negate moving forward

open_comment_speakers.name: Lynn Segal
open_comment_speakers.topic: stop everything with CU and cancel August 21 st forum as well

agenda_items.section: CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL
agenda_items.title: CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Acting Mayor Havlick called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. and attendance was recorded.

agenda_items.title: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND COUNCIL/STAFF RESPONSE
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council heard public participation and City Manager Bruno responded.

agenda_items.title: CONSENT AGENDA
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council approved consent items 3A through 3G, 5 0, Eldridge, Morzel and Toor absent.

agenda_items.title: APPROVAL OF CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES FROM JULY 15, 2003.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Approved as part of consent items 3A through 3G.

agenda_items.title: CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION APPROVING THE YOUTH OPPORTUNITIES PROGRAM ANNUAL GRANTS FUND 2003-2004 ALLOCATIONS.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Approved as part of consent items 3A through 3G.

agenda_items.title: CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION TO GRANT A TEN YEAR LEASE TO MUSTARD’S LAST STAND, INC. FOR 757 SQUARE FEET LOCATED AT 1719 BROADWAY STREET FOR RESTAURANT PURPOSES.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Approved as part of consent items 3A through 3G.

agenda_items.title: INTRODUCTION, FIRST READING AND CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION TO ORDER PUBLISHED BY TITLE ONLY AN ORDINANCE AMENDING SECTIONS 2-10-8, 2-10-12, 2-10-13, AND 2-10-14, B.R.C. 1981 CONCERNING INVESTMENT OF CITY FUNDS, TO REFLECT CHANGES IN STATE LAW, IN THE TERMINOLOGY USED FOR FEDERAL SECURITIES AND BY SECURITIES RATING AGENCIES.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Approved as part of consent items 3A through 3G.

agenda_items.title: INTRODUCTION, FIRST READING AND CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION TO ORDER PUBLISHED BY TITLE ONLY AN ORDINANCE DESIGNATING THE STRUCTURES AND THEIR SITE LOCATED AT 2045 WALNUT, ALSO KNOWN AS THE GUTFELDER HOUSE AND MASON TERRACE, AS INDIVIDUAL LANDMARKS UNDER THE CITY OF BOULDER HISTORIC PRESERVATION CODE. APPLICANT: SUE MUNDINGER.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Approved as part of consent items 3A through 3G.

agenda_items.title: INTRODUCTION, FIRST READING AND CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION TO ORDER PUBLISHED BY TITLE ONLY AN ORDINANCE CONCERNING THE LOCAL AMENDMENTS TO B.R.C. 1981, TITLE 10 “STRUCTURES ADOPTING THE 2003 INTERNATIONAL CODES,” AND THE 2002 NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE AND REVISING CHAPTER 10-5 “BUILDING CODE,” 10-6 “ELECTRICAL CODE,” 10-8 “FIRE PREVENTION CODE,” 10-9 “MECHANICAL CODE,” 10-10 “PLUMBING CODE,” AND ADDING CHAPTERS 10-5.5 “INTERNATIONAL RESIDENTIAL CODE,” AND 10-9.5 “INTERNATIONAL FUEL GAS CODE.”
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Approved as part of consent items 3A through 3G.

agenda_items.title: INTRODUCTION, FIRST READING AND CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION TO ORDER PUBLISHED BY TITLE ONLY AN ORDINANCE SUBMITTING TO THE QUALIFIED ELECTORS OF THE CITY OF BOULDER AT THE GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 4, 2003, THE COUNCIL DISTRICTING AND DIRECT ELECTION OF THE MAYOR CHARTER INITIATIVE, SETTING FORTH THE BALLOT TITLE, AND PROVIDING OTHER DETAILS IN RELATION THERETO.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Approved as part of consent items 3A through 3G.

agenda_items.title: PUBLIC HEARINGS
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council considered Ordinance No. 7299 and the IAFF arbitration report.

agenda_items.title: SECOND READING AND CONSIDERATION OF ORDINANCE No. 7299 AMENDING CHAPTER 5-8, “WEAPONS,” B.R.C. 1981, TO CONFORM TO CHANGES IN STATE LAW, ALLOW THE CITY MANAGER TO PROHIBIT DEADLY WEAPONS IN CITY BUILDINGS, AND REPEAL PROVISIONS CONCERNING CONCEALED WEAPONS PERMITS.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council adopted Ordinance No. 7299, 6:0, Eldridge and Toor absent.

agenda_items.title: CONSIDERATION OF A MOTION REGARDING THE INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF FIREFIGHTERS (IAFF) ARBITRATION REPORT.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council voted 6 0 to implement the last best offer by the City to IAFF Local 900, Eldridge and Toor absent.

agenda_items.title: MATTERS FROM THE CITY MANAGER
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council received updates on Floral Drive speed bumps, water supplies and CU South.

agenda_items.title: UPDATE REGARDING FLORAL DRIVE SPEED BUMPS.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council concurred with accepting the neighborhood petition indicating 82% approval for retaining the devices.

agenda_items.title: DROUGHT UPDATE AND REPORT ON WATER SUPPLIES.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council received the water supply and water rate study updates and requested the current level of water reserves.

agenda_items.title: REPORT ON DISCUSSIONS CONCERNING THE FLATIRONS PROPERTY/CU SOUTH.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council discussed CU South; the motion to invite the CU Regents to an initial dialogue later failed 2 4.

agenda_items.title: MATTERS FROM THE CITY ATTORNEY
agenda_items.outcome_summary: NONE

agenda_items.section: MATTERS FROM MAYOR AND MEMBERS OF COUNCIL
agenda_items.title: MATTERS FROM MAYOR AND MEMBERS OF COUNCIL
agenda_items.outcome_summary: No action was taken on the potential call-up, and Havlick asked about the Shanahan Ridge loop Skip route.

agenda_items.section: MATTERS FROM MAYOR AND MEMBERS OF COUNCIL
agenda_items.title: POTENTIAL CALL-UPS
agenda_items.outcome_summary: No action was taken on the Wonderland Creek Trail connection permit.

agenda_items.title: WONDERLAND CREEK TRAIL CONNECTION, WONDERLAND CREEK, SOUTH OF ELKS CLUB – FLOODPLAIN DEVELOPMENT PERMIT. WIP DATE: 7/24/03, LAST OPPORTUNITY FOR CALL-UP: AUG. 5, 2003, STAFF APPROVAL.
agenda_items.outcome_summary: No action was taken on this item

agenda_items.title: PUBLIC COMMENT ON MATTERS
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council heard comments from Lynn Segal and Rick Woodsome on CU matters.

agenda_items.title: FINAL DECISIONS ON MATTERS
agenda_items.outcome_summary: The motion to invite the CU Regents to an initial dialogue failed 2 4; Corson, Poinsatte, Riggle and Ruzzin opposed; Eldridge and Toor absent.

agenda_items.title: ADJOURNMENT
agenda_items.outcome_summary: The meeting was adjourned at 9:59 P.M. by motion regularly adopted.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Corson moved, seconded by Ruzzin to approve consent items 3A through 3G
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 5 0, Eldridge, Morzel and Toor absent

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Morzel moved, seconded by Corson to adopt Ordinance No. 7299 amending Chapter 5-8, "Weapons," B.R.C. 1981, to conform to changes in state law, allow the city manager to prohibit deadly weapons in city buildings, and repeal provisions concerning concealed weapons permits.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 6:0, Eldridge and Toor absent

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Corson moved, seconded by Riggie, to implement the last best offer by the City to IAFF Local 900.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 6 0; Eldridge and Toor absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Havlick moved, seconded by Morzel to invite the CU Regents to participate in an initial dialogue with hopes of re-establishing regular interactions.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 2 4; Corson, Poinsatte, Riggle and Ruzzin opposed; Eldridge and Toor absent

motions.motion_text: There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED AT 9:59 P.M..
